_doc: Playbook governance layer (docs/design/playbook-governance-layer.md). Every number and enum the layer uses lives here; nothing in playbooks/ carries its own. Playbook definitions are per vertical in config/playbooks/<vertical>.json.

fact_triggers._doc: Triggers on recorded facts rather than communications, for every vertical. trigger.kpi = [{code, op, value, periods?}] reads the account's latest kpi_measurements (periods = that many latest readings must all breach); trigger.date = {field, within_days | overdue_by_days} reads a date in the account profile. roles, kpi and date are ANDed; a trigger needs at least one of them.

automation_levels.1: playbooks declared approval=auto (notify only) are approved by policy at evaluation time
automation_levels.2: notify and schedule steps are approved by policy once a human has approved that playbook's plan (per playbook version)
automation_levels.3: notify and schedule steps are approved by policy on their own; escalations and offers need a human
automation_levels.4: escalations are approved by policy too and marked for a human to review afterwards; offers need a human

autonomy._doc: How far policy may act without a human, for every vertical. A tenant has one level plus optional per-action-class levels; each is capped by ceiling / ceiling_by_class (the platform's limit: an FDE chooses at or below it). policy_approves[level] = the action classes policy may approve at that level. At level 1 only playbooks declared approval=auto qualify; at the levels in needs_plan_approval a human must have approved that playbook version once for the tenant. always_human wins over every level: those action classes, any playbook or step that declares one of those effects, and any account carrying a flag the vertical's playbook file lists under always_human.account_flags. A declined proposal or a failed report lowers the level of that action class by lower_by (never below lower_floor); only a person raises a level again. suggest_raise_after = the run of human approvals with no decline or failure after which a raise is suggested (never applied).

business_events._doc: The business transaction log (models.BusinessEvent, playbooks/events.py): one row per playbook event, written in the same transaction as the change. read_scope_by_role = who may read it in the app: 'tenant' (every event of the tenant) or 'own_accounts' (events on the user's assigned accounts, plus tenant-level settings events); a role not listed cannot read it. Tenant keys over MCP read the whole tenant.
